title: Daybreak SE implementation scratchbook - Xenith Health
content:
Quick morning dump — things to keep top of mind for Xenith Health Private deployment (notes / TODOs / config fragments).

Context: Xenith needs a VPC-hosted Private deployment in us-west-2, FISMA-like controls, HSM-backed key management, and can accept multi-tenant inference within a single VPC using strict network segmentation. They want deterministic 99th pctl latency for chat endpoints and an A/B rollout between quantized 4-bit and FP16 variants.

Today objectives:
- Finalize network security checklist for infra team (see firewall rules below).
- Lock KMS/HSM ownership model and backup rotation cadence with security.
- Validate that model pinning + automatic fallback works when dedicated pool saturates.
- Start canary rollout config for chat route (route: /v1/chat/xenith-qa).

Morning blockers / open questions:
- HSM vendor needs list of acceptable vendors. Security asked for compliance matrix (FIPS/CAVP). Priya to follow up.
- Customer asked whether we can expose per-route token-level billing in their internal billing UI; product says yes but need a short sample payload and guidance.
- Do we have a documented approach for exposing model variant metadata to customer's telemetry? (Trace ID mapping for model-version -> yes/no?)

Action items (short):
1) Samir: draft firewall/security checklist and share with infra by EOD (JIRA:SE-4798).
2) Priya: KMS ownership doc + HSM options (due 2026-03-11).
3) John: run regression on latency for 4-bit quantized 2.7B vs fp16 2.7B using sequence profile from Xenith (ticket INF-2130).
4) Maya: prepare canary rollout JSON and validation hooks for Drift detection.
5) All: sync tomorrow 10:30 PT with Xenith infra team (30m).

Notes / fragments to copy into formal doc later:
- Firewall rules (baseline):
  - Allow egress from inference hosts to: 10.0.0.0/16 (control plane), 0.0.0.0:443 (downloads to mirrors), 10.2.0.0/24 (monitoring).
  - Deny inbound to inference hosts except: bastion IPs + internal load balancer health-checks (443).
  - Open ephemeral ports for KV cache sync (tcp 12000-12010) between nodes — restrict to SGs in same VPC.

- KMS/HSM pattern:
  - Customer-managed KMS key in their AWS account. Redwood reads via cross-account IAM role with kms:Decrypt only for service principal.
  - HSM requirement -> bring-your-own-HSM (AWS CloudHSM) integration plan: we mount a dedicated HSM cluster, Redwood uses signing operations only.
  - Backup: snapshot of key metadata, no plaintext export. Rotation: annual, triggerable via Redwood Console API.

- Model pinning & fallback behavior (implementation sketch):
  - route-config: {"pinned_model": "redwood/model-xenith-v1-fp16", "fallback_order": ["quant-4bit-v1","model-xenith-v0.9-fp16"], "sla": {"p99_ms": 250}}
  - On capacity shortfall -> runtime attempts routing to first compatible fallback respecting quantization compatibility table.
  - Metrics we emit: model.requested, model.served, model.fallback_count, fallback_latency_ms.

- Canary rollout checklist (mini):
  - Canary weight 5% (first day), 25% (3rd day), 50% (7th day) -> manual stop at any quality regression.
  - Perf gates: p95 latency delta < 10% and p99 < 20% vs baseline FP16 for same QPS.
  - Quality gates: automated eval on 250 sample prompts; fail if Rouge-L or semantic-similarity falls below threshold.

Quick commands / snippets I ran locally (keep record):
- perf harness: ./run_perf.sh --model quant-4bit-v1 --seq 512 --qps 20 --duration 10m --out /tmp/xenith-quant-run1.log
- kv cache sync check: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://private.console.local/xenith/kv/status | jq .last_sync

Draft canary JSON (very rough) to paste into Console template:
{
  "route": "/v1/chat/xenith-qa",
  "allocations": [
    {"model": "redwood/model-xenith-v1-fp16", "weight": 95},
    {"model": "redwood/model-xenith-v1-quant4", "weight": 5}
  ],
  "gates": {
    "latency_p95_pct": 10,
    "latency_p99_pct": 20,
    "eval_sample_set": "xenith-canary-250"
  }
}

UX notes for customer onboarding doc:
- Keep model names stable in telemetry for 30 days post-rollout.
- Provide a simple toggle in their UI for 'prefer cheaper model variants' (maps to routing policy).

Random troubleshooting notes (past incidents):
- Observed KV cache inconsistency when sequence length bursts > 1024 for more than 5m — appears to be because node eviction schedules misalign under GC pressure. Mitigation: bump cache TTL + stagger refresh windows.

Unresolved questions to file into ticket INF-2130:
- What is acceptable fallback semantics for stateful chat sessions? If fallback switches model mid-session, do we need to rehydrate KV cache or tag user warnings?
- Are we allowed to log prompt text in customer logs for debugging? Need explicit consent clause.

Things I want to add to final runbook:
- Step-by-step VPC peering + route table entries (with screenshots).
- Sample IaC snippets (terraform) to create cross-account KMS role and trust policy.
- Mini-troubleshooting flowchart for cache divergence and model-fallback incidents.

End-of-day quick checklist (mark when done):
- [ ] firewall checklist posted to infra JIRA
- [ ] canary JSON checked into PR
- [ ] KMS options emailed to security
- [ ] schedule follow-up with Xenith for 2026-03-13 10:30 PT

Notes-to-self: keep this doc noisy and unformatted until we have a repeatable pattern. Move cleaned sections to Confluence under private-deploy-patterns when stable.

-- Samir
